body:
### Microsoft PowerToys version

0.89.0

### Installation method

WinGet

### Running as admin

Yes

### Area(s) with issue?

Mouse Without Borders

### Steps to reproduce

Coincidentally, I noticed that MWB creates log files in three different locations:

1. One log file per day named `Log_YYYY-MM-DD.txt` in the folder `~\AppData\Local\Microsoft\PowerToys\MouseWithoutBorders\Logs\0.89.0.0`
2. Another log file per day named `mouseWithoutBorders-log_YYYY-MM-DD.txt` in the folder `~\AppData\Local\Microsoft\PowerToys\MouseWithoutBorders\LogsModuleInterface`
3. Several log files per day in the folder `C:\Windows\System32\config\systemprofile\AppData\Local\Microsoft\PowerToys\MouseWithoutBorders\Logs\0.89.0.0\`

Also, there doesn't seem to be a process that cleans up these logs from time to time, so I had already collected several hundred of these files.

The files that I checked contained only INFO level messages, so it is questionable whether they should be logged by default anyway.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

1. MWB should write logs to only one folder (ideally not the `Windows` system folder?)
2. MWB should have some cleanup process that removes logs periodically (e. g. logs older than 30 days are removed at startup?)

title: Add greater than to the possible key remapping
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

Hi,
in **Powertoys Keyboard Manager** remaping the  "<" key is straghtforward but ">" must be done by using SHIFT+ combination for "<". (not very intuitive)

I am writing this from a laptop keyboard that (for some strange reason) does not have "<" nor ">" but i have seen  some keyboards where the combination is exactly AltGr +z for "<" and AltGr+x for ">".

For ease of use ">" should be added to the possible key mappings, this way people could map AltGr +z for "<" and AltGr+x for ">" and possibly use stickers to show the mappings on the keyboard. 


PS:Congrats on the powertoys tools.

### Scenario when this would be used?

"<" and ">" are keys that need to be easily acessible for coding, math formulas, teaching...

This change would make it possible to use keyboard stykers in the usual place reserved for the AltGr combination and visually help users find the keys.

### Supporting information

Seen numerous post on this subject missing "<" and ">" on keyboard many people seem to never even find the SHIFT "trick" in powertoys to get the ">" sign.

Other tools seem to offer this possibility but if anything is altering keyboard related, i think Microsoft should be the (safest) way.

body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

According to https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/31967#issuecomment-2004228551 , the performance of the PowerToys Run page is getting worse with every addition to the types of settings plugins can declare.

> I think we should consider refactoring the Plugins settings XAML. There's so much XAML that's being loaded at all times now for every plugin, but half of these would not use something like CheckboxAndMultilineTextBox. The Run settings page is already pretty slow to load.
We should add an ItemsControls / ListView and use a DataTemplateSelector to swap out the template that a specific setting would need: this would also make it easier to maintain and easier to further extend in the future. We are doing the same thing for the Dashboard page where cards have can have different templates.

### Scenario when this would be used?

Makes it easier to maintain and improves UI performance.

title: [BugReport Tool] Update GPO reports to include new PT Run plugin GPOs
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

After implementing #25438 (#27468) we have to update the GPO report in BugReport tool. Because this policies are not static we can't simply query their method in gpo.h as we don't have a list of plugin IDs.

I suggest to simply do a Registry export of the following keys:
- HKCU\Software\Policies\PowerToys
- HKLM\Software\Policies\PowerToys

We need the following keys / values included in the report:
- The value "PowerLauncherAllPluginsEnabledState" in "HKCU\Software\Policies\PowerToys" and "HKLM\Software\Policies\PowerToys".
- All entries with name and value in "HKCU\Software\Policies\PowerToys\PowerLauncherIndividualPluginEnabledList" and "HKLM\Software\Policies\PowerToys\PowerLauncherIndividualPluginEnabledList".

### Scenario when this would be used?

Having problems with policies.

_Note: Because we log the policy state of the plugins in the log file of PT Run this enhancement is no must have for the v0.75.0 release._

title: "Find My Mouse" is *very* surprising and confusing
body:
### Description of the new feature / enhancement

I'm not sure if this is a bug or an enhancement, but "Find My Mouse" creating a circle when you accidentally double-pless ctrl is very surprising, especially if you *triple* press ctrl and it vanishes before you can see what it's doing - you just momentarily see a circle and your screen flashes.  It's not obvious it's coming from the mouse and at first I thought it was some accidental screenshot utility or something.  Powertools installs a large suite of software and so it would not have occurred to me that this circle comes from one of the many tools it brought in -- I installed Powertools for the image-resizer explorer extension, which has a much more discoverable and explicit UI.  

See replies here of various users that were similarly surprised and confused (and one absolutely terrible person who **suggested a system restore to correct the issue**):

https://answers.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/forum/all/when-pressing-ctrl-randomly-a-white-circle-thing/4cdadca7-e011-4679-9f1b-567ea1790365?rtAction=1686237774031

Or just google "ctrl white circle" and you'll see countless people confused where this came from and asking how to remove it.

"Find my mouse" is a good feature now that I understand it and I like using it, but it's easy to trigger accidentally and is worrying when I don't know what it is or what action I performed to cause it.  I don't have a specific request on how to fix the problem, but I would definitely like the feature to re-thought to be less surprising.

Maybe improve the triple press behavor?  Or have it *start* from the mouse and pulse outwards instead of zooming in from the outside?  At least then it would be clear that this is a mouse-related utility.  Or maybe launch a toast notification when it's used with an option to remove the toast notification?

### Scenario when this would be used?

Any new user of PowerTools who did not explicitly review every tool within it or choose it specifically for Find My Mouse and who frequently taps the ctrl key would probably find this useful and less confusing.

### Supporting information
